report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2 of daedalus/eval/correctness.py covering git helpers, pytest node argv, ANSI-aware parser, PytestRun dataclass, and _spawn_pytest.
risks: _spawn_pytest | medium | ManagedProcess fallback to subprocess.run may lose containment silently if CancellationUnavailable is not imported correctly | test with spine disabled
_spawn_pytest | medium | Output file placed in a tempdir that may not be cleaned up on error | verify tempdir removal logic
_same_node | low | Suffix matching may match unintended nodes if requested is a prefix of another node | review test cases with overlapping node names

Add test for ANSI escape handling in parse_pytest_output with FORCE_COLOR=3

claims.text: Deliberately close to ``spine.attempt.pytest_gate_argv``: the same interpreter and the same ``-p no:cacheprovider``
claims.why: The comparison to spine.attempt.pytest_gate_argv is not visible in this chunk; the claim about identical interpreter and flag cannot be verified.

claims.text: ``--color=no`` is NOT cosmetic and was NOT here before 2026-07-30.
claims.why: The function includes --color=no in its return tuple (line ~328). The historical claim is uncheckable but the presence is verified.

claims.text: pytest normally suppresses colour when its output is not a tty, so a captured pipe was assumed to be clean. It is not: pytest honours ``FORCE_COLOR`` (and ``PY_COLORS``) regardless of whether anyone is watching
claims.why: The code includes --color=no to override FORCE_COLOR/PY_COLORS, confirming the assumption was false and this is the fix.

claims.text: The parser strips escapes too (see :data:`_ANSI_RE`). Both are deliberate: this function controls its own invocation and asks for clean output, while the parser is a pure function that may be handed output it did not invoke.
claims.why: _ANSI_RE is defined and used in parse_pytest_output to strip escapes before matching. The docstring explains the dual approach.

claims.text: The full CSI form rather than just ``\x1b\[[0-9;]*m``: pytest also emits cursor and erase-line sequences, and a parser that handles only colour would be correct until the day the terminal width changed.
claims.why: _ANSI_RE = re.compile(r"\x1b\[[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~]") matches full CSI sequences including cursor and erase, not just color codes.

claims.text: A node the output says nothing about is ``not_run`` -- not a pass, not a fail.
claims.why: Initialization sets statuses[q] = STATUS_NOT_RUN for all requested nodes; nodes with no matching lines retain that value.

claims.text: An explicit ``not found`` (``missing``) is final and outranks everything, because the node does not exist
claims.why: After processing, missing nodes are set to STATUS_MISSING last, overwriting any previous status (lines ~470-472).

claims.text: otherwise several report lines for one node reduce to the WORST outcome seen (see ``_STATUS_RANK``)
claims.why: In the loop, when a match is found, the status is updated if current is STATUS_NOT_RUN or observed rank > current rank (lines ~452-455).

claims.text: a node with no line of its own inherits ``collect_error`` if its FILE failed to collect.
claims.why: After the loop, nodes still at STATUS_NOT_RUN whose file matches a file_error are set to STATUS_COLLECT_ERROR (lines ~459-462).

claims.text: Preferred path is :class:`daedalus.spine.cancel.ManagedProcess`, i.e. a Windows Job Object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, so a hung or forking test tree dies with the run
claims.why: The implementation tries to import ManagedProcess and uses it if available, but the claim about KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: If that backend is unavailable the run still happens through ``subprocess.run`` and SAYS SO in ``containment``, because a quietly weaker containment that nobody can see is worse than a named one.
claims.why: When ManagedProcess is not available or CancellationUnavailable is raised, subprocess.run is used and containment remains 'none' (lines ~510-514).

claims.text: Output goes to a file OUTSIDE the worktree: a pipe deadlocks on a chatty run while the parent is polling instead of reading
claims.why: Output is written to a file in a temporary directory (tmpdir / 'pytest.out'), not piped. The code opens out_path and passes the file handle as stdout.

claims.text: Three spellings have to compare equal, and all three were measured on this box rather than assumed: ... a PARAMETRIZED test is requested as ``file.py::test_x`` and reported as ``file.py::test_x[1]``, once per case.
claims.why: The function checks r.startswith(q + "[") or ("/" + q + "[") in r, matching parametrized suffixes.

claims.text: Windows spells the same file two ways, so it is case-insensitive
claims.why: Both reported and requested are lowercased before comparison: r, q = _norm_node(reported).lower(), _norm_node(requested).lower().

observations.what: parse_pytest_output does not handle the case where a node appears in both missing and uncollectable; missing wins because it is applied last, but this is implicit.

_spawn_pytest imports CancellationUnavailable and ManagedProcess inside a try block, but if the import fails, CancellationUnavailable is set to Exception and ManagedProcess to None; the subsequent isinstance check may not catch all cases.
_spawn_pytest uses subprocess.STDOUT for stderr, merging stderr into stdout; the docstring does not mention this detail.
The temporary directory created by tempfile.mkdtemp is never explicitly removed in this chunk; cleanup responsibility is unclear.
